hero.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran for Second Time in Three Days
hero.body:
The United States conducted new airstrikes on southern Iran, marking the second such attack within three days. A U.S. official said the strikes targeted attack drones and a drone ground-control station.

The official said the attacks were carried out in self-defense. Targets included four one-way attack drones launched by Iran, according to the official.

The strikes occurred during a fragile cease-fire between the U.S. and Iran. The hostilities threaten the tenuous truce that has been in place during protracted negotiations to end a three-month war.

The attacks come as diplomatic efforts to broker a potential cease-fire hang in the balance. Oil prices jumped following the strikes, with traders concerned about potential disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global energy supplies.

President Trump said he feels no political pressure to reach a deal with Iran, dismissing concerns about upcoming midterm elections. He described Iran as negotiating on fumes and suggested he could outwait the country.

Meanwhile, Israel has ramped up military operations in Lebanon, where clashes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah have intensified in the south. Few in Lebanon believe that diplomatic efforts to end the wider regional war will bring peace to their country, even if the U.S. and Iran reach an agreement.

After 88 days of a near-total internet shutdown, Iran has begun allowing people to connect with the world again. The government had imposed censorship on news, television, and chat services. However, not everyone has access to the restored internet, and those who do are uncertain how long the access will last.

The renewed strikes represent a setback for efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region. The three-month conflict has already had widespread economic and humanitarian consequences across the Middle East.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Rise
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after suspected cases of a rare Ebola type surged.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola concerns escalate in the region. Seven confirmed cases have been identified in Kampala, Uganda's capital.

The outbreak in eastern Congo has grown significantly, with suspected cases exceeding 900 and 119 suspected deaths reported. Uganda's health officials have activated disease surveillance systems to contain the virus's spread, following measures similar to those employed during the COVID-19 pandemic.

cards.headline: Former CIA official arrested after $40 million in gold bars found at home
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA officer with stealing approximately 300 gold bars worth $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole approximately 300 gold bars from the intelligence agency.

According to court documents, Rush allegedly defrauded the government by lying about his credentials. The case represents one of the largest known thefts from a US intelligence agency in recent history.

cards.headline: Paper mill disaster in Longview could be Washington state's deadliest industrial accident
cards.teaser: An explosion at a paper mill in Longview left multiple workers missing and feared dead after a chemical tank ruptured.
cards.body:
A tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview on Tuesday has left two people dead and nine others missing and presumed dead, according to authorities. The Longview fire department confirmed that one person who was hospitalized following the disaster later died.

The incident has drawn comparisons to the deadliest industrial tragedies in modern Washington state history, according to the governor. Emergency response efforts have transitioned from rescue to recovery operations as crews search for the missing workers.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on prediction markets
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged a longtime Google employee with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer made $1.2 million from the trades, according to the charges.

The case represents a new application of insider trading laws to prediction markets, which allow users to bet on the outcomes of real-world events. Prosecutors allege the Google employee accessed internal data through his position at the company and used that information to gain an unfair advantage when placing bets on the platform.

Polymarket has grown in popularity as a platform where users can wager on everything from election outcomes to corporate announcements. The markets are designed to aggregate information and predict future events, but they rely on participants trading based on publicly available information rather than confidential data.

The charges indicate that federal authorities view the use of insider information on prediction markets the same way they treat traditional securities trading. Insider trading laws prohibit individuals from trading based on material, nonpublic information that could affect the value of securities or, in this case, the outcome of prediction market contracts.

The Google engineer worked at the company for several years before the alleged trades took place. Prosecutors say he violated his duty to keep internal company information confidential by using it for personal financial gain.

The case could set a precedent for how prediction markets are regulated and how insider trading laws apply to new forms of financial platforms. As these markets have grown, questions about their oversight and potential for abuse have increased.

The employee faces federal charges that could result in significant fines and prison time if convicted. Google has not publicly commented on the case or the employee's current status with the company.

cards.headline: Georgia Coach Kirby Smart Says He Would Support SEC Leaving the NCAA
cards.body:
Georgia head football coach Kirby Smart said he would support the Southeastern Conference breaking away from the NCAA to operate under its own rules. Smart made the comments as SEC leaders gathered for their spring meetings.

Multiple reports indicated the suggestion came amid ongoing debates about the governance structure of college athletics. ESPN reported that Smart hinted at SEC secession as expansion arguments continue to brew within college sports. The Athletic quoted Smart as saying he would back the SEC playing by its own rules.

The comments came as the SEC held its spring meetings, which Fox News described as turning into a blunt reality check for broken college athletics. The possibility of the conference operating independently from the NCAA represents a significant potential shift in how major college sports could be organized.

Yahoo Sports published an analysis questioning the viability of such a move, arguing that going solo would lead to the death of the SEC. The piece suggested that breaking away from the broader NCAA structure could create unforeseen challenges for the conference.

The idea of major conferences leaving the NCAA has circulated in college sports discussions as administrators grapple with questions about athlete compensation, transfer rules, and competitive balance. The SEC is one of the most powerful conferences in college athletics, particularly in football, where its programs generate substantial revenue.

Smart's willingness to endorse a breakaway reflects broader frustrations among coaches and administrators about current NCAA governance. The comments add a prominent coaching voice to discussions that have primarily involved conference commissioners and university presidents.

The timing of the remarks coincided with other major developments in college sports governance. Senators introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reforming college athletics, including proposals for salary caps and transfer limits. CBS Sports reported that SEC leaders discussed contingencies in light of the proposed bill.

No formal proposal for SEC independence from the NCAA has been presented. Smart's comments represent his personal view rather than an official conference position. However, the public endorsement from one of college football's most successful active coaches adds weight to conversations about restructuring college athletics governance.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition in her civil case against President Trump.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times.

Prosecutors are examining whether Carroll committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump. Specifically, they are investigating statements Carroll made about whether she received outside financial support for her legal battles.

cards.headline: Record Spring Heat Wave Hits Europe
cards.teaser: An exceptionally early heat wave is breaking temperature records across the United Kingdom, Spain, and France.
cards.body:
An exceptional spring heat wave is sweeping across Western Europe, shattering temperature records in major cities. London has experienced temperatures reaching 95 degrees over consecutive days, while heat records are breaking across the continent. The extreme conditions have triggered government warnings and resulted in deaths in some areas.

Meteorologists attribute the unprecedented heat to a buckled jet stream driving the warm weather pattern across Europe. Experts note that unpredictable and extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent, part of broader climate disruptions affecting multiple regions globally.

cards.headline: Lebanon Braces for Prolonged Conflict Despite Diplomatic Efforts
cards.teaser: Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah intensify in southern Lebanon as residents lose faith in peace talks.
cards.body:
Few in Lebanon believe that diplomatic efforts to end the wider war will bring peace to their country. Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in the south, even as U.S. and Iranian negotiators work toward a potential agreement.

Israel has ramped up its military operations in Lebanon in recent days. Lebanese residents have resigned themselves to a long war, doubting that any deal between the U.S. and Iran will translate into peace on the ground.

cards.headline: Stock markets close at record highs as oil prices fall on Iran war hopes
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all reached new peaks amid optimism about potential negotiations.
cards.body:
Major US stock indexes reached record highs Monday as investors responded to progress toward a US-Iran peace deal. Oil prices fell sharply, with Brent crude dropping 6% to $97.43 a barrel—its lowest level in two weeks—as markets priced in reduced concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

The decline in energy costs boosted market sentiment, though the impact is already being felt elsewhere. UK energy regulator Ofgem's new price cap will see typical households pay £221 more annually for energy, reflecting the broader effects of the regional conflict on global energy markets.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to explain compliance on tariff refunds
cards.teaser: A judge demanded the customs chief appear at a hearing about efforts to repay $166 billion owed from illegally imposed tariffs.
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the head of US Customs to address compliance issues related to refunding tariffs at an upcoming hearing. The order suggested new concern about the Trump administration's progress in repaying the full $166 billion owed to importers from tariffs that were ruled illegal.

The demand for the customs chief to appear in person was described as surprising and indicated the court may be losing patience with the pace of refunds. The tariffs in question were imposed during the Trump administration and later found to violate trade law, requiring the government to return the collected funds to affected businesses.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam chemicals
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a lawsuit against 3M over contamination caused by PFAS chemicals in firefighting foam used at military sites.
cards.body:
Australia filed a $2 billion lawsuit against 3M, the largest legal claim of its kind in the country. The government is seeking damages to cover costs related to PFAS contamination at 28 defence bases caused by firefighting foam supplied by the American manufacturer.

PFAS chemicals, commonly called "forever chemicals," persist in the environment without breaking down. The Australian government alleges that 3M's products contaminated multiple military installations, necessitating significant cleanup operations.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's motion to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit, clearing the way for a trial in July.
cards.body:
A California court has declined to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency against Tesla. The decision allows the case to proceed, with trial scheduled for July.

The civil rights agency welcomed the ruling and said it is prepared to present its case at trial. The lawsuit alleges that Tesla engaged in discrimination against workers at its California facilities.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell Introduce Bipartisan College Sports Reform Bill
cards.teaser: Two key senators proposed legislation addressing salary caps, transfer limits, and other major changes to college athletics.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced a bipartisan bill aimed at reforming college sports. The legislation, called the Protect College Sports bill, proposes implementing a salary cap and transfer limits for college athletes.

Yahoo Sports reported the bill targets coach poaching, specifically mentioning Lane Kiffin's move to LSU. ESPN noted the proposal includes provisions for eligibility and cap enforcement. CBS Sports indicated SEC leaders discussed contingency plans in response to the bill during their meetings.

cards.headline: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Released From Jail, No Charges Filed
cards.teaser: Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs was arrested on domestic violence charges but released as prosecutors delayed a charging decision.
cards.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail after his arrest on domestic violence allegations. The district attorney has not yet filed formal charges against him.

The investigation into the incident remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Internet After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is letting people reconnect with the world after a near-total internet blackout.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access after 88 days of censored news, television, and chat services. The government imposed a near-total internet shutdown that isolated the country from the world.

Not everyone has regained access to the internet, and those who have are uncertain how long it will last. The shutdown had blocked Iranians from communicating with the outside world and accessing uncensored information during the three-month war.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over $1.2 million in prediction market trades
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a Google staffer with using insider information to profit from trades on the Polymarket platform.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly made $1.2 million in profits on Polymarket bets related to Search-related trends in 2025. According to the unsealed complaint, Spagnuolo knew the outcomes of these wagers before the trading public because he had accessed Google's confidential information.

The case represents the second known federal criminal charge involving alleged insider trading on prediction market platforms, underscoring growing government enforcement efforts in this emerging sector.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric car faces criticism from investors and Italy
cards.teaser: The new model drew memes, analyst skepticism, and a stock selloff after its unveiling.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first fully electric car, the Luce model, has sparked divided reactions following its unveiling. The company's stock fell as investors expressed concerns about the vehicle's market appeal. The new model divided opinion on social media, with some questioning whether it aligns with Ferrari's traditional brand identity.

The backlash reflects broader challenges facing the luxury automaker as it navigates the shift toward electric vehicles amid competition from Chinese EV makers.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 for first R2 SUV deliveries to customers
cards.teaser: Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for its first R2 SUV customer deliveries. The electric vehicle maker has spent years developing the new model ahead of this initial rollout.

CEO RJ Scaringe has emphasized the significance of the R2, calling it potentially the most important product Rivian has launched. The SUV marks an important expansion of the company's lineup as it moves beyond its initial truck and SUV offerings.

cards.headline: Google's AI fails to spell basic words including company's own name
cards.teaser: Google's AI search tool has shown ongoing problems correctly spelling common words like Google, disregard, stop, and ignore.
cards.body:
Google's artificial intelligence search feature has struggled to spell basic words, including the company's own name. The AI has had particular difficulty with words like "disregard," "stop," and "ignore."

The spelling problems have affected Google's AI-generated search results, prompting some users to reconsider whether competing search engines like Microsoft's could offer a viable alternative. Google has acknowledged the issues and is working to address how its AI handles certain words and instructions.

cards.headline: SEC Leaders Criticize College Football Playoff Metrics Explanation
cards.teaser: Southeastern Conference officials criticized the explanation of metrics used by the College Football Playoff committee as strength of schedule debates continue.
cards.body:
Leaders from the Southeastern Conference blasted the College Football Playoff's explanation of its metrics amid intensifying debate over strength of schedule. Sports Illustrated reported the criticism from SEC officials focused on how the playoff committee evaluates teams.

The dispute centers on the methodology used to assess strength of schedule when selecting teams for the expanded playoff. SEC leaders expressed dissatisfaction with the transparency and consistency of the metrics explanation provided by playoff officials.

cards.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Not Use AI as Final Word on Creative Decisions
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he finds AI useful for solving medical problems but opposes its use in creative processes within Hollywood.

Spielberg drew a clear line about where he believes AI should stop in the entertainment industry. He said he does not want the technology taking over creative decision-making in film production.

The director has not publicly elaborated on specific examples of AI use in Hollywood that concern him. His comments come as the entertainment industry debates how to integrate artificial intelligence into various aspects of production, from script analysis to visual effects.

Spielberg's position adds his voice to ongoing discussions about technology's role in creative industries. The director has built a career spanning decades on human-driven storytelling and filmmaking techniques.

The podcast appearance offered Spielberg a platform to share his views on emerging technology in entertainment. His stance reflects concerns among some industry veterans about preserving human creativity in an era of advancing automation.

While acknowledging potential benefits of AI in other fields, Spielberg made clear his opposition to letting algorithms make final creative choices in filmmaking. His comments suggest a preference for keeping human judgment at the center of artistic decisions in Hollywood productions.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News in Mike Wallace Scholarship Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: A high school senior used his News Emmy scholarship acceptance to challenge CBS News leadership.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior from District of Columbia International School in Washington, addressed the News Emmys audience while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship. He criticized CBS News, saying the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship named after the network's late journalist. Campos delivered his remarks during the ceremony honoring news programming achievements.

cards.headline: U.S. military strikes Iranian drone site amid ongoing peace talks
cards.body:
The U.S. military struck an Iranian ground control station and shot down four Iranian attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to U.S. officials. The military also attacked an Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground.

U.S. Central Command said in a statement that its forces shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones that posed a threat in the area. A senior U.S. official said the military struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas, a port city on Iran's southern coast, that was preparing to launch a fifth drone.

The incident marks the second such military clash in 48 hours between the two countries. Iran's military fired the four drones at a commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz before U.S. forces intercepted them, according to a senior U.S. official speaking on condition of anonymity.

The strikes occurred as the United States and Iran are engaged in negotiations to end their ongoing conflict. President Trump had indicated over the weekend that an agreement was close, but his remarks at a Cabinet meeting on Wednesday differed from those earlier statements.

During the Cabinet meeting, Trump maintained what officials described as maximum demands on Iran, signaling a harder line than his weekend comments suggested. The president did not elaborate on the specific terms being discussed in the negotiations.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical shipping channel through which a significant portion of global oil supplies pass. Attacks on commercial vessels in the waterway have raised concerns about freedom of navigation and energy security.

U.S. Central Command has not released additional details about the commercial ship targeted by the Iranian drones or whether it sustained any damage. The military characterized the Iranian drones as posing a threat to vessels in the area.

The timing of the military action complicates the diplomatic effort to reach an agreement between Washington and Tehran. Neither the White House nor Iranian officials have publicly commented on how the latest clash might affect the ongoing peace talks.

cards.headline: Former federal judges challenge Trump IRS settlement in court filing
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group argues the administration circumvented the court by negotiating a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges filed a court motion Wednesday asking that President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service be reopened. The judges argue the administration bypassed proper judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement outside the courtroom.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended for individuals who claim they were wronged by the government. The former judges contend this arrangement circumvented necessary court supervision of the case.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court petition
cards.teaser: Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while he appeals his case against the Trump administration to the nation's highest court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free on Tuesday as he pursues his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court. The 3rd Circuit issued the order.

The three-judge panel included Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman and Thomas Hardiman, who were appointed by President Trump, former President George W. Bush and former President Joe Biden, respectively.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said his country has not yet built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to provide Patriot missile interceptors to assist Ukraine in its conflict with Russia.

Zelensky acknowledged that Ukraine has made progress defending against drone attacks but lacks the domestic capacity to produce anti-missile defense systems domestically.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Husband Was Having a Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought her husband might have suffered a stroke while watching the debate unfold.

In a clip from the CBS interview set to air Sunday, Biden said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, emphasizing how alarmed she felt during the debate.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after contentious Texas Senate primary
cards.teaser: Republican party leaders are rebuilding relationships with Ken Paxton following a divisive primary campaign in Texas.
cards.body:
Republican officials are rebuilding their relationship with Ken Paxton following a divisive Texas Senate primary. The primary runoffs have now concluded, setting the stage for the general election matchup.

Democrat Talarico is preparing to challenge Paxton in November, centering his campaign on scandals linked to the Republican candidate. The race has drawn attention at the highest levels, with President Trump discussing it during a Cabinet meeting.

cards.headline: FIFA under investigation over World Cup ticket pricing and seat locations
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey authorities are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The probe examines whether FIFA's sales methods violated consumer protection laws in the two states, which will host multiple matches.

Fans have reported being misled about ticket sales and seat locations, purchasing tickets for specific areas only to find their actual seats were elsewhere in the stadiums.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution as it passed the planet on its way to study a metal-rich asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed photographs of Mars during a flyby of the red planet. The probe took images including views of Mars' south pole as it traveled toward its destination, a metal-rich asteroid.

The spacecraft used the Mars flyby as part of its journey to study the asteroid Psyche in the main asteroid belt. The images provide new perspectives of the Martian surface captured during the spacecraft's trajectory.

cards.headline: Dodgers Place Kiké Hernández Back on Injured List With Oblique Tear
cards.teaser: Los Angeles placed infielder Kiké Hernández on the injured list with a significant oblique tear just two games after his return.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers returned Kiké Hernández to the injured list after diagnosing him with a significant oblique tear. MLB Trade Rumors reported the tear as significant, while ESPN said Hernández went back to the IL with the oblique injury.

MLB.com reported Hernández returned to the injured list after playing just two games following his previous absence. The Dodgers recalled a player from Triple-A to replace him on the roster. The Los Angeles Times had reported Hernández's emotional comeback before the setback occurred.

cards.headline: ABC News Wins Eight Awards at News Emmys, Including Top Prize for World News Tonight
cards.teaser: ABC News repeated its victory for outstanding live news program at the 47th annual News Emmys.
cards.body:
ABC News dominated the 47th annual News Emmys with eight wins overall. The network claimed the top prize for outstanding live news program for ABC World News Tonight With David Muir, marking back-to-back victories in this category.

National Geographic also had a strong showing with seven News Emmys. The network's success was bolstered by multiple wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller, which emerged as a standout performer at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Morris Day Says He Will Not Perform at Freedom 250 Festival Despite Being Listed
cards.teaser: The musician denied plans to perform at a National Mall concert celebrating the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied rumors that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall in Washington. The event is part of a 16-day patriotic celebration in the nation's capital.

Organizers had previously announced Day as a headliner for the show. Other performers listed for the festival include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. The event has drawn attention for its association with the current administration.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Responds to Criticism Over Recent Fashion Choices
cards.teaser: The singer addressed online backlash about her clothing after internet commenters criticized her recent outfits.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo responded to criticism about her recent fashion choices. Internet commenters accused her outfits of both infantilizing and sexualizing the singer.

Rodrigo said people should not be held responsible for someone else sexualizing them. The singer addressed the online backlash directly in her public comments about the dress controversy.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Becomes Emotional Honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: The late-night host called the podcaster his life partner during a Hollywood Walk of Fame speech.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel grew teary-eyed while presenting Adam Carolla with his Hollywood Walk of Fame star on Wednesday. During his speech, Kimmel described Carolla as his "life partner," noting that the affectionate description carried genuine meaning.

The two first met in 1994 while working together on Kevin and Bean, a Los Angeles radio show. Their friendship and professional relationship have endured since those early radio days.

cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought her husband might have suffered a stroke while watching the debate unfold.

In a clip from the CBS interview set to air Sunday, Biden said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, emphasizing how alarmed she felt during the debate.

The case represents the second known federal criminal charge involving alleged insider trading on prediction market platforms, underscoring growing government enforcement efforts in this emerging sector.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on prediction markets
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged a longtime Google employee with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer made $1.2 million from the trades, according to the charges.

The case represents a new application of insider trading laws to prediction markets, which allow users to bet on the outcomes of real-world events. Prosecutors allege the Google employee accessed internal data through his position at the company and used that information to gain an unfair advantage when placing bets on the platform.

Polymarket has grown in popularity as a platform where users can wager on everything from election outcomes to corporate announcements. The markets are designed to aggregate information and predict future events, but they rely on participants trading based on publicly available information rather than confidential data.

The charges indicate that federal authorities view the use of insider information on prediction markets the same way they treat traditional securities trading. Insider trading laws prohibit individuals from trading based on material, nonpublic information that could affect the value of securities or, in this case, the outcome of prediction market contracts.

The Google engineer worked at the company for several years before the alleged trades took place. Prosecutors say he violated his duty to keep internal company information confidential by using it for personal financial gain.

The case could set a precedent for how prediction markets are regulated and how insider trading laws apply to new forms of financial platforms. As these markets have grown, questions about their oversight and potential for abuse have increased.

The employee faces federal charges that could result in significant fines and prison time if convicted. Google has not publicly commented on the case or the employee's current status with the company.

cards.headline: Stock markets close at record highs as oil prices fall on Iran war hopes
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all reached new peaks amid optimism about potential negotiations.
cards.body:
Major US stock indexes reached record highs Monday as investors responded to progress toward a US-Iran peace deal. Oil prices fell sharply, with Brent crude dropping 6% to $97.43 a barrel—its lowest level in two weeks—as markets priced in reduced concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

The decline in energy costs boosted market sentiment, though the impact is already being felt elsewhere. UK energy regulator Ofgem's new price cap will see typical households pay £221 more annually for energy, reflecting the broader effects of the regional conflict on global energy markets.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to explain compliance on tariff refunds
cards.teaser: A judge demanded the customs chief appear at a hearing about efforts to repay $166 billion owed from illegally imposed tariffs.
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the head of US Customs to address compliance issues related to refunding tariffs at an upcoming hearing. The order suggested new concern about the Trump administration's progress in repaying the full $166 billion owed to importers from tariffs that were ruled illegal.

The demand for the customs chief to appear in person was described as surprising and indicated the court may be losing patience with the pace of refunds. The tariffs in question were imposed during the Trump administration and later found to violate trade law, requiring the government to return the collected funds to affected businesses.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric car faces criticism from investors and Italy
cards.teaser: The new model drew memes, analyst skepticism, and a stock selloff after its unveiling.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first fully electric car, the Luce model, has sparked divided reactions following its unveiling. The company's stock fell as investors expressed concerns about the vehicle's market appeal. The new model divided opinion on social media, with some questioning whether it aligns with Ferrari's traditional brand identity.

The backlash reflects broader challenges facing the luxury automaker as it navigates the shift toward electric vehicles amid competition from Chinese EV makers.

cards.headline: FIFA under investigation over World Cup ticket pricing and seat locations
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey authorities are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The probe examines whether FIFA's sales methods violated consumer protection laws in the two states, which will host multiple matches.

Fans have reported being misled about ticket sales and seat locations, purchasing tickets for specific areas only to find their actual seats were elsewhere in the stadiums.

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam chemicals
hero.teaser: The Australian government filed a lawsuit against 3M over contamination caused by PFAS chemicals in firefighting foam used at military sites.
hero.body:
Australia filed a $2 billion lawsuit against 3M, the largest legal claim of its kind in the country. The government is seeking damages to cover costs related to PFAS contamination at 28 defence bases caused by firefighting foam supplied by the American manufacturer.

PFAS chemicals, commonly called "forever chemicals," persist in the environment without breaking down. The Australian government alleges that 3M's products contaminated multiple military installations, necessitating significant cleanup operations.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's motion to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit, clearing the way for a trial in July.
cards.body:
A California court has declined to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency against Tesla. The decision allows the case to proceed, with trial scheduled for July.

The civil rights agency welcomed the ruling and said it is prepared to present its case at trial. The lawsuit alleges that Tesla engaged in discrimination against workers at its California facilities.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 for first R2 SUV deliveries to customers
cards.teaser: Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for its first R2 SUV customer deliveries. The electric vehicle maker has spent years developing the new model ahead of this initial rollout.

CEO RJ Scaringe has emphasized the significance of the R2, calling it potentially the most important product Rivian has launched. The SUV marks an important expansion of the company's lineup as it moves beyond its initial truck and SUV offerings.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution as it passed the planet on its way to study a metal-rich asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed photographs of Mars during a flyby of the red planet. The probe took images including views of Mars' south pole as it traveled toward its destination, a metal-rich asteroid.

The spacecraft used the Mars flyby as part of its journey to study the asteroid Psyche in the main asteroid belt. The images provide new perspectives of the Martian surface captured during the spacecraft's trajectory.

cards.headline: Google's AI fails to spell basic words including company's own name
cards.teaser: Google's AI search tool has shown ongoing problems correctly spelling common words like Google, disregard, stop, and ignore.
cards.body:
Google's artificial intelligence search feature has struggled to spell basic words, including the company's own name. The AI has had particular difficulty with words like "disregard," "stop," and "ignore."

The spelling problems have affected Google's AI-generated search results, prompting some users to reconsider whether competing search engines like Microsoft's could offer a viable alternative. Google has acknowledged the issues and is working to address how its AI handles certain words and instructions.

hero.headline: Georgia Coach Kirby Smart Says He Would Support SEC Leaving the NCAA
hero.body:
Georgia head football coach Kirby Smart said he would support the Southeastern Conference breaking away from the NCAA to operate under its own rules. Smart made the comments as SEC leaders gathered for their spring meetings.

Multiple reports indicated the suggestion came amid ongoing debates about the governance structure of college athletics. ESPN reported that Smart hinted at SEC secession as expansion arguments continue to brew within college sports. The Athletic quoted Smart as saying he would back the SEC playing by its own rules.

The comments came as the SEC held its spring meetings, which Fox News described as turning into a blunt reality check for broken college athletics. The possibility of the conference operating independently from the NCAA represents a significant potential shift in how major college sports could be organized.

Yahoo Sports published an analysis questioning the viability of such a move, arguing that going solo would lead to the death of the SEC. The piece suggested that breaking away from the broader NCAA structure could create unforeseen challenges for the conference.

The idea of major conferences leaving the NCAA has circulated in college sports discussions as administrators grapple with questions about athlete compensation, transfer rules, and competitive balance. The SEC is one of the most powerful conferences in college athletics, particularly in football, where its programs generate substantial revenue.

Smart's willingness to endorse a breakaway reflects broader frustrations among coaches and administrators about current NCAA governance. The comments add a prominent coaching voice to discussions that have primarily involved conference commissioners and university presidents.

The timing of the remarks coincided with other major developments in college sports governance. Senators introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reforming college athletics, including proposals for salary caps and transfer limits. CBS Sports reported that SEC leaders discussed contingencies in light of the proposed bill.

No formal proposal for SEC independence from the NCAA has been presented. Smart's comments represent his personal view rather than an official conference position. However, the public endorsement from one of college football's most successful active coaches adds weight to conversations about restructuring college athletics governance.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell Introduce Bipartisan College Sports Reform Bill
cards.teaser: Two key senators proposed legislation addressing salary caps, transfer limits, and other major changes to college athletics.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced a bipartisan bill aimed at reforming college sports. The legislation, called the Protect College Sports bill, proposes implementing a salary cap and transfer limits for college athletes.

Yahoo Sports reported the bill targets coach poaching, specifically mentioning Lane Kiffin's move to LSU. ESPN noted the proposal includes provisions for eligibility and cap enforcement. CBS Sports indicated SEC leaders discussed contingency plans in response to the bill during their meetings.

cards.headline: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Released From Jail, No Charges Filed
cards.teaser: Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs was arrested on domestic violence charges but released as prosecutors delayed a charging decision.
cards.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail after his arrest on domestic violence allegations. The district attorney has not yet filed formal charges against him.

The investigation into the incident remains ongoing.

cards.headline: SEC Leaders Criticize College Football Playoff Metrics Explanation
cards.teaser: Southeastern Conference officials criticized the explanation of metrics used by the College Football Playoff committee as strength of schedule debates continue.
cards.body:
Leaders from the Southeastern Conference blasted the College Football Playoff's explanation of its metrics amid intensifying debate over strength of schedule. Sports Illustrated reported the criticism from SEC officials focused on how the playoff committee evaluates teams.

The dispute centers on the methodology used to assess strength of schedule when selecting teams for the expanded playoff. SEC leaders expressed dissatisfaction with the transparency and consistency of the metrics explanation provided by playoff officials.

cards.headline: Dodgers Place Kiké Hernández Back on Injured List With Oblique Tear
cards.teaser: Los Angeles placed infielder Kiké Hernández on the injured list with a significant oblique tear just two games after his return.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers returned Kiké Hernández to the injured list after diagnosing him with a significant oblique tear. MLB Trade Rumors reported the tear as significant, while ESPN said Hernández went back to the IL with the oblique injury.

MLB.com reported Hernández returned to the injured list after playing just two games following his previous absence. The Dodgers recalled a player from Triple-A to replace him on the roster. The Los Angeles Times had reported Hernández's emotional comeback before the setback occurred.

hero.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Not Use AI as Final Word on Creative Decisions
hero.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he finds AI useful for solving medical problems but opposes its use in creative processes within Hollywood.

Spielberg drew a clear line about where he believes AI should stop in the entertainment industry. He said he does not want the technology taking over creative decision-making in film production.

The director has not publicly elaborated on specific examples of AI use in Hollywood that concern him. His comments come as the entertainment industry debates how to integrate artificial intelligence into various aspects of production, from script analysis to visual effects.

Spielberg's position adds his voice to ongoing discussions about technology's role in creative industries. The director has built a career spanning decades on human-driven storytelling and filmmaking techniques.

The podcast appearance offered Spielberg a platform to share his views on emerging technology in entertainment. His stance reflects concerns among some industry veterans about preserving human creativity in an era of advancing automation.

While acknowledging potential benefits of AI in other fields, Spielberg made clear his opposition to letting algorithms make final creative choices in filmmaking. His comments suggest a preference for keeping human judgment at the center of artistic decisions in Hollywood productions.

cards.headline: ABC News Wins Eight Awards at News Emmys, Including Top Prize for World News Tonight
cards.teaser: ABC News repeated its victory for outstanding live news program at the 47th annual News Emmys.
cards.body:
ABC News dominated the 47th annual News Emmys with eight wins overall. The network claimed the top prize for outstanding live news program for ABC World News Tonight With David Muir, marking back-to-back victories in this category.

National Geographic also had a strong showing with seven News Emmys. The network's success was bolstered by multiple wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller, which emerged as a standout performer at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News in Mike Wallace Scholarship Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: A high school senior used his News Emmy scholarship acceptance to challenge CBS News leadership.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior from District of Columbia International School in Washington, addressed the News Emmys audience while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship. He criticized CBS News, saying the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship named after the network's late journalist. Campos delivered his remarks during the ceremony honoring news programming achievements.

cards.headline: Morris Day Says He Will Not Perform at Freedom 250 Festival Despite Being Listed
cards.teaser: The musician denied plans to perform at a National Mall concert celebrating the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied rumors that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall in Washington. The event is part of a 16-day patriotic celebration in the nation's capital.

Organizers had previously announced Day as a headliner for the show. Other performers listed for the festival include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. The event has drawn attention for its association with the current administration.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Responds to Criticism Over Recent Fashion Choices
cards.teaser: The singer addressed online backlash about her clothing after internet commenters criticized her recent outfits.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo responded to criticism about her recent fashion choices. Internet commenters accused her outfits of both infantilizing and sexualizing the singer.

Rodrigo said people should not be held responsible for someone else sexualizing them. The singer addressed the online backlash directly in her public comments about the dress controversy.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Becomes Emotional Honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: The late-night host called the podcaster his life partner during a Hollywood Walk of Fame speech.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel grew teary-eyed while presenting Adam Carolla with his Hollywood Walk of Fame star on Wednesday. During his speech, Kimmel described Carolla as his "life partner," noting that the affectionate description carried genuine meaning.

The two first met in 1994 while working together on Kevin and Bean, a Los Angeles radio show. Their friendship and professional relationship have endured since those early radio days.

hero.headline: U.S. military strikes Iranian drone site amid ongoing peace talks
hero.body:
The U.S. military struck an Iranian ground control station and shot down four Iranian attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to U.S. officials. The military also attacked an Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground.

U.S. Central Command said in a statement that its forces shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones that posed a threat in the area. A senior U.S. official said the military struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas, a port city on Iran's southern coast, that was preparing to launch a fifth drone.

The incident marks the second such military clash in 48 hours between the two countries. Iran's military fired the four drones at a commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz before U.S. forces intercepted them, according to a senior U.S. official speaking on condition of anonymity.

The strikes occurred as the United States and Iran are engaged in negotiations to end their ongoing conflict. President Trump had indicated over the weekend that an agreement was close, but his remarks at a Cabinet meeting on Wednesday differed from those earlier statements.

During the Cabinet meeting, Trump maintained what officials described as maximum demands on Iran, signaling a harder line than his weekend comments suggested. The president did not elaborate on the specific terms being discussed in the negotiations.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical shipping channel through which a significant portion of global oil supplies pass. Attacks on commercial vessels in the waterway have raised concerns about freedom of navigation and energy security.

U.S. Central Command has not released additional details about the commercial ship targeted by the Iranian drones or whether it sustained any damage. The military characterized the Iranian drones as posing a threat to vessels in the area.

The timing of the military action complicates the diplomatic effort to reach an agreement between Washington and Tehran. Neither the White House nor Iranian officials have publicly commented on how the latest clash might affect the ongoing peace talks.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition in her civil case against President Trump.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times.

Prosecutors are examining whether Carroll committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump. Specifically, they are investigating statements Carroll made about whether she received outside financial support for her legal battles.

cards.headline: Former federal judges challenge Trump IRS settlement in court filing
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group argues the administration circumvented the court by negotiating a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges filed a court motion Wednesday asking that President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service be reopened. The judges argue the administration bypassed proper judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement outside the courtroom.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended for individuals who claim they were wronged by the government. The former judges contend this arrangement circumvented necessary court supervision of the case.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court petition
cards.teaser: Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while he appeals his case against the Trump administration to the nation's highest court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free on Tuesday as he pursues his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court. The 3rd Circuit issued the order.

The three-judge panel included Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman and Thomas Hardiman, who were appointed by President Trump, former President George W. Bush and former President Joe Biden, respectively.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said his country has not yet built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to provide Patriot missile interceptors to assist Ukraine in its conflict with Russia.

Zelensky acknowledged that Ukraine has made progress defending against drone attacks but lacks the domestic capacity to produce anti-missile defense systems domestically.
